text:
maria: quick writeup from the kv stride-reservation + evictor throttle run. uploaded logs: gs://redwood-perf/kv/3923456789

hao: short summary — the new stride-reservation evictor + throttle eliminated the OOM noise during the afternoon spike. OOM count: 5 -> 0. tradeoff: p99 token latency for short-chat workload up ~12%. overall throughput roughly same.

devin: profiling notes: kernel routing started favoring the small-matmul path for seq <= 128 once reserve hits 15%. that path has a slightly larger workspace (coral-kernel) due to extra scratch buffers — ~40MB/GPU increase. I attached flamegraph links in the gcs folder.

hao: config we used in the run:
```
{
  "evictor": {
    "mode": "stride_reserve",
    "reserve_ratio": "0.18",
    "throttle_ms": "8",
    "per_request_cap_kb": "256",
    "prefill_policy": "aggressive_on_cold_prefixes"
  }
}
```

ben: interestingly, allocator fragmentation went up. reserve allocates fixed stride slots causing free-list scatter when mixed tiny/huge KV entries are present. fragmentation metric (slab_waste) +17%. some of that maps to uncoalesced slab tails.

jen: concern — the p99 regression correlates with short-request batches that hit the throttler and then trigger a kernel swap. the swap adds ~6-12ms due to workspace rebinds. we should avoid full kernel swap for tiny sequences if possible.

maria: can you paste the perf counters that show kernel swap counts?

devin: counters from the run (summarized):
- kernel_swap_count: 1.8k (baseline 200)
- avg_workspace_rebind_ms: 7.2ms
- kv_hit_rate: 82% (baseline 86%)
- slab_waste_bytes: +48MB/GPU

hao: root cause hypothesis: stride reservation prevents eviction for active prefixes, which is good for quality, but causes the allocator to hold fragmented slots. when throttle engages, requests are queued, batching heuristics accumulate slightly larger microbatches which then route to a different kernel optimized for larger batches -> workspace mismatch and rebind.

ben: mitigation ideas:
- variable stride sizes (size-classed reservation) instead of fixed strides
- lighter per-request cap (try 128KB) to reduce oversized KV inserts
- opportunistic coalescing pass during low activity windows to reduce fragmentation

jen: also consider throttle hysteresis: only throttle when workspace pressure > 72% for > 200ms. current throttle is too eager (trips on short spikes).

maria: can we try a 72% hysteresis + per_request_cap=128KB + reserve_ratio=0.12 in canary? small rollout to 10 hosts.

hao: yes. I'll schedule a canary job. expected impact: drop kernel_swap_count ~60%, reduce p99 back ~5-6% above baseline, fragmentation down a bit.

devin: also propose a quick patch to kernel router: prefer in-place small sequence path if workspace_rebind_expected_ms > 4ms. avoids swap for tiny seqs. small patch + unit tests.

reclaim-bot: [AUTOMATION] mem-pressure at 3923456900: triggered reclaim routine, freed 48MB inactive slots on host gpu-3.

maria: tasks: hao -> run canary with new knobs, devin -> open PR for router guard, ben -> prototype coalescer sim for weekend run, jen -> add throttle hysteresis metric and alert. I'll sync tomorrow 10:30. Thanks :thumbsup:

hao: noted. starting canary orchestration now. will post logs and metrics in thread when ready.

devin: will draft the router PR tonight.

ben: I'll push a simple sim in the repo under perf/kv/coalesce-sim and share results by EOD Friday.
